title: Descent, component factorization and discrete comparison for continuous set functions
statement: Use compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $D$ be any topological space and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces with finite jointly surjective coverings, $S\mapsto C(S,D)$ is a sheaf of sets. The continuous-function presheaf $F_{D,X}(U)=C(|U|,D)$ with restriction by precomposition [def-sfb-continuous-set-presheaf] is a sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. If $D$ is totally disconnected and $U$ is a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] scheme over $X$, the connected-component quotient $q_U:|U|\to\pi_0(|U|)$ has profinite target, and precomposition is a bijection $C(\pi_0(|U|),D)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|U|,D)$, natural in $U$ and continuous maps of $D$. Here $\pi_0$ has the quotient topology. If $D$ is discrete, the map from the constant presheaf with value $D$ to $F_{D,X}$, sending $d$ to the constant function $d$, is locally surjective and locally injective: sections lift on an open covering and two constants with equal images are equal on a covering. Its sheafification is an isomorphism from the associated constant set sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to $F_{D,X}$. This includes $D=\varnothing$ and the empty scheme.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 4.2.12, p.30; HRS Example 3.1, p.6; former item steps 1, 2 and 9.

proof.text: For a finite jointly surjective family $S_i\to S$ of profinite spaces put $S\prime=\coprod_i S_i$ and $q:S\prime\to S$. A finite disjoint union is compact: restrict an open cover to each summand, take a finite subcover there, and unite these finitely many finite subcovers. The cited compact-to-Hausdorff theorem therefore makes $q$ a quotient map. A compatible family $f_i:S_i\to D$ defines a continuous $f\prime:S\prime\to D$ by its summand restrictions. Compatibility on $S_i\times_S S_j$ says $f_i(x)=f_j(y)$ whenever $x,y$ have the same image in $S$. Thus $f\prime$ is constant on every fibre of $q$, and defines a unique set map $f:S\to D$. For each open $O\subseteq D$, $q^{-1}(f^{-1}(O))=(f\prime)^{-1}(O)$ is open. The quotient criterion makes $f^{-1}(O)$ open, so $f$ is continuous and glues the family. Surjectivity of $q$ gives uniqueness. If the family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $S=\varnothing$ and there is exactly one map $S\to D$, as required. No separation condition on $D$ was used. In Lean this is the existing Mathlib construction continuousSetProfiniteSheaf, whose property is the required sheaf condition; TopCat.toSheafCompHausLike proves it by quotient descent.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2(1), proof, first sentence (continuous surjections of profinite sets are quotient maps); expanded finite-family argument

proof.text: The fpqc sheaf of sets of the cited theorem has sections $C(|U|,D)$ and precisely the precomposition restrictions of $F_{D,X}$. Every covering in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an fpqc covering by its site definition. A matching family on such a cover, including its agreement on the scheme fibre products over $U$, therefore has a unique continuous-map section over $U$ by fpqc descent. This section is a section of $F_{D,X}$ itself. This proves the sheaf condition on the generating coverings, hence on their generated Grothendieck topology. Apply Mathlib isSheaf_fpqcTopology_continuousMapPresheaf, Presheaf.IsSheaf.of_le with Scheme.proetaleTopology_le_fpqcTopology, and the continuous forgetful functor op_comp_isSheaf_of_isSheaf.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, first assertion and first paragraph of proof; use its fpqc strengthening already recorded in the DAG

proof.text: If $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its underlying space is spectral by the cited scheme theorem. Apply the spectral-component theorem to $|U|$: its quotient $\pi_0(|U|)$ by connected components, with the quotient topology, is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected. This is the claimed profinite target. This step does not require any hypothesis on $D$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12 and the paragraph immediately following its proof; Stacks Tags 094L and 0906

proof.text: Assume $D$ totally disconnected. A continuous image of a connected component $K$ of $|U|$ is connected: a separation of the image would pull back to two disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets covering $K$. By total disconnectedness this image has at most one point. Every $f\in C(|U|,D)$ is therefore constant on each component and defines a unique set map $\bar f:\pi_0(|U|)\to D$ with $\bar f q_U=f$. It is continuous directly from the quotient topology: for open $O\subseteq D$, $q_U^{-1}(\bar f^{-1}(O))=f^{-1}(O)$ is open. Conversely $g\mapsto gq_U$ is continuous precomposition; the two operations are inverse because $q_U$ is surjective. For $a:V\to U$, the same connected-image argument defines $\pi_0(a)$ and $q_U|a|=\pi_0(a)q_V$; its continuity follows by the same quotient criterion. Thus $(gq_U)|a|=(g\pi_0(a))q_V$. For continuous $b:D\to D\prime$ between totally disconnected targets, $b(gq_U)=(bg)q_U$. These equalities prove the two stated naturalities. On empty $U$ both function sets are singletons. Lean uses the inverse of continuousMapPresheafEquivOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace for the bijection, Continuous.connectedComponentsMap_mk for scheme naturality, and reflexivity for coefficient naturality.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, second paragraph of proof; quotient-topology and naturality details expanded

proof.text: For each point x of a site object U and continuous section s to a discrete space D, let W_x be the open fibre of s through x. Its inclusion into U is an open immersion, hence etale and weakly etale by the Mathlib instances. Composition with U to X is weakly etale by Mathlib WeaklyEtale.comp, so W_x is a site object. The family indexed by points of U is jointly surjective: x is the image of the point x in W_x. Mathlib Scheme.ofArrows_mem_precoverage_iff makes the underlying family a Zariski precover. Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage makes it a weakly-etale quasi-compact precover. By Scheme.ProEt.precoverage, Presieve.map_ofArrows, and Precoverage.generate_mem_toGrothendieck, it generates a covering sieve on the small pro-etale site. This uses the existing Mathlib open-cover admissibility theorem instead of the stronger project etale/ind-etale comparison packages. When U is empty the family is empty, still jointly surjective, and gives the empty covering.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, discrete-target conclusion; open-cover admissibility expanded

proof.text: Let $D$ be discrete and let $P$ be the constant set presheaf with value $D$. The functions $\eta_U(d)(u)=d$ define a presheaf map $\eta:P\to F_{D,X}$, since precomposition preserves constants. For $f\in C(|U|,D)$, each fibre $W_d=f^{-1}(\{d\})$ is open. The nonempty fibres cover $U$, and on $W_d$ the section $f$ is the image of $d\in P(W_d)$. Step 5 makes this an allowed covering. If $D=\varnothing$, a section $f$ exists only when $U=\varnothing$; the empty covering gives local surjectivity there without choosing an element of $D$. If $\eta_U(d)=\eta_U(e)$ and $U$ is nonempty, evaluation at any point of $U$ gives $d=e$, so the identity covering witnesses local injectivity. On empty $U$, the empty covering witnesses local injectivity, even for unequal $d,e$. Thus $\eta$ is locally surjective and locally injective, with no exception for empty $D$ or $U$. The Lean family is indexed by points x of U, with value s(x), rather than by all elements of D; its universe is therefore u even when D has universe u+1. For local injectivity Mathlib Scheme.ProEt.bot_mem_topology supplies the empty covering.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, last assertion; fibre-open-cover and empty-case details expanded

proof.text: Use the small-skeleton and compatible-universe convention of the site. Apply the cited set-presheaf local-bijection criterion to $\eta$ from step 6: its sheafification $P^\#\to F_{D,X}^\#$ is an isomorphism. By step 2 the target presheaf is already a sheaf, so its sheafification is canonically itself (the universal property gives mutually inverse maps). By the definition of the constant set sheaf, $P^\#$ is the associated constant sheaf $\underline D$. The resulting isomorphism $\underline D\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{D,X}$ is the one induced by the constant functions $d\mapsto\eta(d)$. In Lean W_of_isLocallyBijective and W_iff show that presheafToSheaf.map of the constant-section map is invertible. Adjunction.homEquiv_counit identifies continuousSetConstantMap with this map followed by the invertible sheafification counit.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, last assertion, completed using the set-valued sheafification criterion

lean.statement: theorem continuousSet_descent_components (X : Scheme.{u}) (D : Type (u + 1)) [TopologicalSpace D] : Presheaf.IsSheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) (ContinuousMap.yonedaPresheaf (CompHausLike.compHausLikeToTop (fun T ↦ TotallyDisconnectedSpace T)) D) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (continuousSetPresheaf X D) ∧ (∀ (U : Over X), CompactSpace U.left → QuasiSeparated (toSpecZ U.left) → CompactSpace (ConnectedComponents U.left) ∧ T2Space (ConnectedComponents U.left) ∧ TotallyDisconnectedSpace (ConnectedComponents U.left) ∧ (∀ (_ : TotallyDisconnectedSpace D), Function.Bijective (fun g : C(ConnectedComponents U.left, D) ↦ g.comp ⟨ConnectedComponents.mk, ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe⟩) ∧ (∀ (V : Over X), CompactSpace V.left → QuasiSeparated (toSpecZ V.left) → ∀ (a : V ⟶ U) (g : C(ConnectedComponents U.left, D)), (g.comp ⟨ConnectedComponents.mk, ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe⟩).comp a.left.base.hom = (g.comp ⟨a.left.base.hom.continuous.connectedComponentsMap, a.left.base.hom.continuous.connectedComponentsMap_continuous⟩).comp ⟨ConnectedComponents.mk, ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe⟩) ∧ (∀ (E : Type (u + 1)) [TopologicalSpace E] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace E] (b : C(D, E)) (g : C(ConnectedComponents U.left, D)), b.comp (g.comp ⟨ConnectedComponents.mk, ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe⟩) = (b.comp g).comp ⟨ConnectedComponents.mk, ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe⟩))) ∧ (∀ (_ : DiscreteTopology D), (∀ (U : X.ProEt) (s : C(U.left, D)) (x : U.left), ∃ (W : U.left.Opens) (d : D), x ∈ W ∧ ∀ y : W, s y = d) ∧ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (continuousSetConstantPresheafMap X D) ∧ Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (continuousSetConstantPresheafMap X D) ∧ IsIso (continuousSetConstantMap X D))
